summary.title: Video Generation Models are General-Purpose Vision Learners

details: Computer vision lacks a universal pre-training objective analogous to next-token prediction; existing perception foundation models remain task-specific with custom heads/losses.
Claim: large-scale text-to-video generation is that universal pre-training paradigm (spatio-temporal/physical priors, native vision-language alignment, scalability).

GenCeption: a pre-trained text-to-video diffusion transformer converted into a single-pass feed-forward perception model — clean (noise-free) video latents fed in with timestep fixed at t=0 and the rectified-flow velocity output negated, features taken from the final layer, so no architectural change to the backbone.

Unified task interface: all dense tasks (depth, normals, segmentation, DensePose, camera raymaps) are expressed as 3-channel RGB videos with a single shared decoder and a single L2 loss, and the target task is selected purely by the text prompt; sparse tasks (2D/3D keypoints) use appended learnable per-frame tokens with an MLP head.
Task specification is moved from architecture/loss engineering into data representation (e.g. median-normalized log-compressed depth removes the need for scale-invariant losses).
WAN 2.1 text-to-video diffusion, 1.3B (S) and 14B (L) variants; 81 frames at 480x832, 24 FPS; VAE with 4x temporal / 8x spatial compression.
Adam, lr 5e-5, 15k steps, batch 64 on 256 v6e TPUs; gradient clipping plus gradient dropping for stability; latents and text embeddings precomputed offline.
Inference: single forward pass replaces 50-step sampling — 5.92s (13.6 FPS) / 15.3GB for 1.3B, 10.03s (8.0 FPS) / 42.8GB for 14B per 81-frame clip.
Raymap trick for camera pose: 6-channel ray origins/directions packed into 3 channels by spatial partitioning (origins center, directions periphery).

7.5K self-generated human-centric synthetic videos: 800 RenderPeople assets animated with 200 CMU mocap motions, varied 3D scenes/HDRI backdrops, focal lengths and camera trajectories; GT depth/normals/masks via Blender render passes, joints from rigged assets.
Augmented with TartanAir, Virtual KITTI, MVS-Synth (depth; TartanAir also camera trajectories) — 4 datasets, 8.08K videos, 1.23M frames total.
Only expression-referring segmentation uses real data: MeViS, Ref-COCO, YouTube-VOS.
No training set from any evaluation benchmark is used.
Normals: Sintel, Hi4D (mAE); depth: Sintel, KITTI, ETH3D, Goliath (AbsRel, delta1); camera pose: Sintel (ATE, RPE-T/R).
Soft foreground segmentation: VideoMatte, PhotoMatte85, PPM-100 (MSE); expression-referring segmentation: Ref-DAVIS, MeViS (J&F); 3D human keypoints: EMDB (MPJPE).
Protocols for Hi4D and Goliath follow Sapiens/DAVID; referring segmentation follows VoCap.

Specialist SOTA: DepthAnything3, VGGT / VGGT-Omega, D4RT, MapAnything, Sapiens, DAVID, NormalCrafter, Lotus-2, Marigold-E2E-FT, SAM3 (+Gemini), VoCap, ReferEverything, VISA, RVM/MODNet, Genmo, TRAM, GVHMR; generalist baseline Diception.
Pretraining ablation: same fine-tuning pipeline and data on largest V-JEPA (0.6B) and VideoMAE V2 (0.6B, 1B) backbones.
Ablations on number of transferred pre-trained DiT layers (including from-scratch DiT), specialist vs jointly trained generalist, data-volume and model-size scaling on depth.

key_findings.finding: A single feed-forward model derived from a text-to-video diffusion backbone matches or beats task-specialized state-of-the-art models across dense and sparse video perception tasks, while trained almost entirely on synthetic data.
key_findings.evidence: 14B specialist: Sintel depth AbsRel 0.130 (vs 0.145 VGGT-Omega, 0.148 D4RT), Goliath AbsRel 0.008 (vs 0.012 DAVID), Hi4D normals mAE 10.99 (vs 12.14 Sapiens), Sintel normals 29.7 (vs 30.3 Lotus-2), Sintel camera ATE 0.050 / RPE-T 0.018 (best), MeViS J&F 70.0 and Ref-DAVIS 76.4 (vs 60.3/75.0 ReferEverything, 57.5/64.5 SAM3+Gemini), EMDB MPJPE 71.8 (vs 73.0 Genmo); no benchmark training sets used.

key_findings.finding: Video generative diffusion pre-training yields substantially better perceptual features than masked-prediction or joint-embedding video pre-training under identical fine-tuning.
key_findings.evidence: On the same 7.5K-video/0.9M-frame synthetic set, average depth AbsRel/delta1: V-JEPA-H 0.281/52.2, VideoMAE V2-H 0.175/62.0, VideoMAE V2-G (1B) 0.154/66.9, versus WAN 2.1-S (1.3B) 0.122/85.8 and WAN 2.1-L (14B) 0.093/90.7.

key_findings.finding: The approach is extremely data-efficient and shows preliminary data/model scaling.
key_findings.evidence: With 4 datasets / 8.08K videos / 1.23M frames it reaches average depth AbsRel 0.071 vs VGGT-Omega 0.067 (trained on ~3M videos / ~600M frames) and D4RT 0.082 (~86M frames) — 7x to 500x less data; performance improves monotonically from 1.3B to 14B and from 0.9M to 1.23M frames.

key_findings.finding: Pre-trained weights are the decisive ingredient: a randomly initialized DiT barely learns, and quality rises with the number of transferred pre-trained layers.
key_findings.evidence: Layer-transfer ablation shows a nearly flat learning curve for the from-scratch DiT and monotonically improving performance as more pre-trained layers are loaded.

key_findings.finding: Training only on single-person synthetic videos produces emergent generalization to real footage, multiple instances, and out-of-distribution categories, with detail exceeding the Blender-rendered supervision.
key_findings.evidence: Zero-shot qualitative results on real multi-person videos, animals and anthropomorphic characters; fine structures such as cat whiskers and soft hair mattes are recovered despite absence in training GT.
